transcript: Last night, I saw Water For Elephants on Broadway, a new musical adaptation of the best-selling novel which follows Jacob Jankowski, a veterinarian who has run away with the circus. I had mixed feelings about it but the show is still in previous and I think it can definitely be tightened up. This production uses circus arts as a storytelling device and the stunts and acrobatics are really well done. You can't really see anything like this anywhere else on Broadway right now. Also, the puppetry is very cool and overall direction and the ways the design elements are utilized are really artful. The script has a lot of heart and the performances are great, but I think in general, this production prioritizes the spectacle at the expense of the storytelling while trying to have both. Although the circus acts are meant to enhance the story, some of it definitely feels gratuitous and could be better integrated into the storytelling — some of it doesn't feel quite earned. But on the other hand, the parts with less spectacle, like a lot of Act 2, feel really slow. I kind of attribute this to the score which is fine but not really memorable, and I wish it had allowed the performers to show off more of their vocal abilities. The run time which is currently 2 hours and 45 minutes also did not feel earned to me, but I think at least pacing is something that always improves throughout previews. I'm overall optimistic that this show is heading in the right direction, but I would definitely recommend going for the circus above anything else. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer explicitly states 'mixed feelings' and provides balanced praise for the circus arts and spectacle while criticizing the score, pacing, runtime, and integration of spectacle with storytelling. The recommendation is conditional ('go for the circus above anything else') and the overall tone is cautiously optimistic but not enthusiastic.
